A post-operational monitoring program, proposed by the Applicant, would be initiated in Howard Creek to determine the time needed for the stream to recover from construction effects. If flow augmentation is initiated, water used to augment flow in Howard Creek would be continuously monitored for temperature, dissolved oxygen, and flow rate. Water quality monitoring would not be conducted in Bad Creek Reservoir, since Lake Jocassee would be its principle water source, and because 47 percent of the upper reservoir volume could be recycled daily and up to 90 percent weekly.
The Applicant proposed to take appropriate measures to ensure the health and safety of workers and visitors during construction and operation. The public would be restricted from the project area during construction. The Applicant would comply with regulations and safety procedures required by the Occupational Safety and Health Act. The Applicant has the capability to control mosquito breeding in the project area, should such a problem occur, and would consult with and follow the recommendations of the Medical Entomologist of the South Carolina State Board of Health and Environmental Control on any insect problem. Mosquito problems are not expected to occur during operation of the project, primarily because of the steep shoreline and continuous large fluctuations of water level that are expected in the reservoir under the proposed operating schedules.
In areas of public health concern, such as individual water supplies, waste disposal systems, and solid waste, the Applicant would conform to applicable Federal, State, and local regulations. Methods for handling domestic and solid wastes have been described in earlier sections of this statement.
Upon completion of construction, the entire upper reservoir would be fenced with nonclimbable wire, and signs would be posted along the fence to inform the public of the restricted area.
